story: As an operator, I want a job that checks every privacy promise (deletion windows, export times, consent versions, audio expiry) and a page that shows it, so that a missed promise pages before a learner notices.
acceptance_criteria:
Given a missed window, when `privacy/verify` runs, then `privacy_promise_missed` pages.
Until it ships: the 08:30 checklist runs the privacy checks as SQL (audio older than 15 minutes with storage off, open deletion requests, export requests over 48 hours); the 15-minute deletion itself is automatic (E13-S05).

title: Incident runbook and tabletop
story: As an operator, I want a security incident runbook and a 60-minute tabletop run once before the beta, so that the first incident is not the first rehearsal.
acceptance_criteria: Given the tabletop, when done, then the runbook lists the steps, the contacts, the learner-notice template and the processor list, and the gaps found are fixed or ticketed.

title: Deletion and export requests honoured from day one
story: As a learner, I want "delete my account" and "export my data" to work from my first day, before the automated purge and export jobs exist, so that the promise holds for the first cohort too.
acceptance_criteria:
Given a deletion request (two taps and a typed "delete"), when confirmed, then access ends at once, a `deletion_ledger` row exists and the learner's data key is destroyed, so every audio object becomes unreadable at once; there is no grace period and no restore (ADR-24.B1).
Given the request, when the on-call runs the purge runbook (reviewed SQL by learner id as `forone_purge`, the Langfuse per-user delete, the vendor deletions in the register), then the live purge completes within 24 hours and the runbook checklist is filed with the ledger row; E13-S06 replaces the runbook by its due day.
Given an export request before E13-S06 ships, when made, then the screen says it arrives within 72 hours, and the on-call runs the export runbook (the zip of 04 D16, no passphrase, an emailed link that opens the notebook and mints a 15-minute presigned URL, the file kept 7 days); the 1-hour promise starts when E13-S06 ships (ADR-24.B7).

title: Price book
story: As an operator, I want `prices.yaml` with every vendor's unit prices, dated, and a `price_book` table, so that a price change is a commit and the January rises are already in the plan.
acceptance_criteria: Given a vendor call with no price row, when traced, then it is recorded as `unpriced` and alarms.

title: Tracing middleware and `vendor_calls`
story: As an operator, I want every model, voice and speech call to pass through middleware that records unit usage, price, role, learner (tokenized), episode and cache hit, so that cost is a query from the first test render.
acceptance_criteria: Given the vendor tests in Phase 1, when run, then every render is a priced `vendor_calls` row and "cost per 10 minutes of audio" is real before any episode exists.

title: Session cost roll-up and the per-episode line
story: As an operator, I want `cost/rollup` into `session_costs` per role and vendor, feeding `episodes.cost_usd`, so that the cost report shows where the money goes.
acceptance_criteria: Given 20 test episodes, when rolled up, then teacher, writer, editor and voice lines are shown against the estimate ($0.08, $0.07, $0.03, $0.18).

title: Spend caps and spend mode
story: As an operator, I want a daily spend cap, a per-learner daily cost guard, and `spend_mode` halt wired into the pipeline and call configuration, so that a runaway night cannot bankrupt the beta. Conserve mode is cut under the single-engineer cut list (architecture 08).
acceptance_criteria: Given the cap is reached, when a new vendor call is attempted, then halt refuses non-live calls, live calls finish, and the on-call is paged.

title: Cost alarms
story: As an operator, I want alarms for kind ceilings, unpriced calls, low cache hit, a session over $1.00, p50 over $0.80 for 7 days and daily spend, so that the stop line is seen the day it is crossed.
acceptance_criteria: Given a session over $1.00, when rolled up, then `session_over_alert` fires with the role breakdown.

title: Call cost and the Haiku-host comparison
story: As an operator, I want per-call cost including LiveKit minutes, the host's cache hit rate, and the 50-call run repeated with a Haiku-class host, so that the cheapest host that passes the governor is known.
acceptance_criteria:
Given the comparison, when done, then latency, governor violations and cost per call are in one table for both hosts.
Given no difference in move-contract violations, talk share and the human read, when `eval-gate` passes, then the host flag flips to the Haiku-class host without a further decision (pre-approved, ADR-24.7).

title: Vendor health and the failover drill
story: As an operator, I want vendor health in the alerts and the weekly report (no `/admin/vendors` page under the single-engineer cut list) and a drill that kills the primary voice key for an hour and still ships the night's episodes, so that a vendor outage is survivable.
acceptance_criteria:
Given the drill, when run in the beta, then every episode ships on the secondary and the report records the time to switch.
Until it ships: vendor health is read from the alerts (E15-S04); the secondary voice path itself is Day-1 (E02-S05, E04-S05).

title: Weekly cost report and the exit document
story: As an operator, I want a weekly report (cost per session, per role, per vendor, cache hits, outliers, next week's prices) and, by the end of the build (2027-03-11), the exit document with the measured cost and the costed path to $0.35, so that the beta's gate on cost is a number.
acceptance_criteria: Given the pilot learners' production week, when reported, then measured cost per session is shown beside the $0.64 estimate and each lever to $0.35 has a measured first column; if it is above $0.42 on the 2 and 3 a day plans, the report says so, because that triggers the ADR-24.5 price rule.

title: Logging with the scrub corpus and paging
story: As an operator, I want structured JSON logs with a scrubber tested against a corpus of personal data, Sentry scrubbing, uptime checks and `ops.page()` to Slack, so that no log carries learner text and an outage is seen.
acceptance_criteria: Given the `pii_corpus`, when the scrubber test runs, then zero leaks; given a down check, then a page arrives within 5 minutes.

title: Milestone 0 fixtures imported
story: As an engineer, I want `tools/import_m0.py` to write fixtures (learner files, scripts with hand coverage, editor reads, transcripts and tags, 30 clips, facts, similarity pairs), so that every suite has real data from day one.
acceptance_criteria: Given the import, when run, then every fixture listed in the operations design exists with its source clip's consent checked.

title: Eval suites and the eval gate in CI
story: As an operator, I want suites for fitter, law scan, claim gate, recognizers, editor, writer, pipeline, memory, host governor replay, injection and analyst, with `eval-gate` running the mapped suites on prompt or rule changes, so that a prompt change cannot break law 7 unseen.
acceptance_criteria: Given a host prompt change that adds "that's wrong", when CI runs, then the law scan and governor replay fail the build.
priority: P0 (law scan, governor, editor), P1 (the rest)

title: Alert rules for pipeline, client, call, cost, privacy and crisis
story: As an operator, I want `ops/alerts.yaml` with rules for missed drops, fallback rates, degraded editor, voice failover, slow first sound, slow host replies, governor violations, cost lines, privacy misses and crisis activations, so that the twelve things that go wrong page.
acceptance_criteria: Given an episode not ready before drop, when detected, then a page arrives within 5 minutes with the runbook link.

title: Release manifest, feature flags and the freeze
story: As an operator, I want every release to record code, prompt and bible versions, flags to switch features without a deploy, and the pre-open freeze from 2027-03-15 12:00 to 03-17 12:00 UTC (with no releases 2026-12-31 to 2027-01-02), so that a bad prompt can be traced and pulled.
acceptance_criteria: Given a bad episode, when its release is looked up, then the manifest names every prompt version in it; given the `pull` action, then the episode is removed from Today and the feed.

title: Runbooks, on-call and the tabletop
story: As an operator, I want the twelve runbooks, the one-engineer on-call rota with Better Stack phone escalation for a systemic drop failure (ADR-24.12), the 08:30 checklist and one 60-minute tabletop (failover by hand, pull, re-run after-pass, wrong memory), so that the 05:40 drop failure has a known owner.
acceptance_criteria:
Given the tabletop, when done before the pre-open freeze, then R1 to R4 and R12 were rehearsed and the gaps ticketed.
Given the manual substitutes the release plan lists (section 5), when the beta opens, then each has a runbook line with an owner and a time limit: the purge (24 hours) and the hand export (72 hours, E13-S13), cancel and plan-change requests in Paddle (one working day, E12-S07, E12-S10), the failed-payment grace (E12-S11), a vetoed target (E10-S02), the reviewer's tokenized sheet (E13-S10, E15-S08), and the privacy, measures and gates SQL in the 08:30 checklist (E13-S11, E15-S07, E15-S09); each line is deleted when its story ships.

title: Measures and the admin measures page
story: As an operator, I want the product measures (first sound, pilot time, speech minutes, talk share, worth it, return after gap, false claims, wrong memories, cost) computed daily with readable-from dates, so that the gates can be read at the gate review (2027-04-20, beta day 35) from the first day's data.
acceptance_criteria:
Given the measures page, when opened, then each measure shows its value, its noise and the date it became readable.
Given the event log from the first day, when the measures job first runs, then it back-fills every measure from the open (2027-03-17), including recognizer error by the learner's first language.
Until it ships: the 08:30 checklist runs the measures as SQL on the event log (`forone_readonly`); the job back-fills from the open.

title: Review sampling and the review pages
story: As an operator, I want 10 random episodes per learner per month and a sample of calls queued for a person to read, with names tokenized, so that quality is judged by a human every month.
acceptance_criteria:
Given the review queue, when a reviewer flags an episode, then the flag feeds the editor suite as a new fixture.
Until it ships: as E13-S10: a tokenized sheet of 10 random episodes per learner, made by hand each month.

title: The gates page
story: As an operator, I want one page with every beta gate (trial to paid, week-4 active, sessions a week, speech minutes, recording change, renewal, worth it, cost, false claims, wrong memories, per-language quality) with pass, stop and readable-from, so that the gate review (2027-04-20) is a reading, not a debate.
acceptance_criteria:
Given a gate below its stop line, when readable, then it is shown in plain words with the stop value beside it.
Until it ships: the gates are read by SQL from the measures (runbook line in E15-S06).

title: Synthetic learners and the canary
story: As an operator, I want 3 synthetic learners seeded from pilot files in the build and 50 in the beta, with a weekly canary episode, so that the pipeline is exercised without touching a real learner.
acceptance_criteria: Given the canary fails, when detected, then `canary_failed` pages.

title: Vendor regression and the weekly digest
story: As an operator, I want a weekly digest of measures, cost and incidents, and a quarterly vendor regression run on the fixed fixtures, so that a silent vendor model change is caught.
acceptance_criteria: Given the first regression in beta week 1, when a vendor's score drops beyond the threshold, then an incident is opened.

title: Cohort 1 invited on the open
story: As an operator, I want the first batch of about 50 invites sent from the waitlist on 2027-03-17, with the pilot learners first, so that the beta starts on the day.
acceptance_criteria: Given the batch, when sent, then redemptions, first sound and first spoken sentence are on the measures page the same day.
depends_on: E06-S02, every Day-1 story in E01 to E15

title: Weekly cohorts and the 08:30 checklist
story: As an operator, I want a new batch each week and a daily checklist (drops, fallbacks, cost, pages, review queue), so that the beta runs on a rhythm.
acceptance_criteria: Given a week, when it ends, then the digest shows the cohort's trial-to-paid, sessions, speech minutes and cost.

title: External test at week 0 and week 8
story: As an operator, I want 20 to 30 English learners to take the Duolingo English Test (ADR-24.19) at week 0 and week 8 with the results imported, so that the internal measure is checked against the world.
acceptance_criteria: Given the import page, when results are loaded, then correlation with the internal skill estimates is shown per skill.
depends_on: E09-S07; the sittings booked by the open, 2027-03-17 (A10)

title: P1 features shipped during the beta
story: As a learner, I want round two, the finale, the tape, shadowing, Apple and Google sign-in and the dial-in experiment to arrive during the beta, so that the product grows while I use it.
acceptance_criteria: Given each P1 story, when shipped, then it goes out behind a flag with its suite passing and is noted in the digest.

title: First false-claim audit and wrong-memory count
story: As an operator, I want the first monthly false-claim audit on beta day 31 (2027-04-16) and the wrong-memory rate read weekly, so that the trust gates are read from real data.
acceptance_criteria: Given the audit, when done, then the rate is on the gates page (target under 5%) with the retractions made.

title: First season finales from beta day 28
story: As a learner who started on 2027-03-17, I want my finale on my first session on or after day 28, with the next goal set inside it, so that season one ends with something to hear.
acceptance_criteria: Given the first finales, when produced, then each has at most two measured differences or an honest "too early to say", and the next goal is stored.

title: Per-language quality and the close rule
story: As an operator, I want worth-it, false-claim and recognizer-error rates per target language and per learner first language, and a rule that closes a language that falls well behind until fixed, so that opening many languages never means shipping a bad one.
acceptance_criteria: Given a language open (a target, or a first language whose speakers learn English), when its worth-it rate is more than 15 points below the English-target average for two weeks, or its recognizer error is well behind, then it closes to new learners and the digest says why.

title: Cost path executed: batch voices and the January prices
story: As an operator, I want batch text-to-speech and the January voice plan executed during the beta, so that cost moves toward $0.35 while the beta runs.
acceptance_criteria: Given the week of 28 December, when the next-week-prices report runs, then the January rises are in it and the measured cost per session is below $0.60.

title: Gate review on 2027-04-20
story: As an operator, I want a one-page reading of every gate against its pass and stop lines, with the failed claim named if any, so that the decision is made on the day.
acceptance_criteria: Given the gates page, when snapshotted on 2027-04-20 (beta day 35), then each gate is pass, fail or not readable, and the document names the one change each failure implies.

title: Season two plan (2027-04-21 to 05-18)
story: As an operator, I want the first post-beta season planned from the gate review: public prices confirmed, the floor stack migrated piece by piece behind blind tests, the observer tested behind a flag, and the second language opened if it passed, so that the beta's lessons become the launch.
acceptance_criteria: Given the review, when the plan is written, then each item has a gate it depends on and a date.

title: The host answers within about a second
story: As a learner, I want the host to reply within about a second of my turn ending, so that the call feels like a conversation.
acceptance_criteria:
Given the 50 scripted calls, when measured, then reply latency median is under 1.5 s and p95 under 2.5 s, and connect is under 3 s.
Given production, when a day's calls are measured, then `host_reply_p50` over 1.5 s for an hour pages.

title: First sound in under 60 seconds, first sentence in under 5 minutes
acceptance_criteria: Given a first open on a 4G phone, when measured on the pilot learners' re-onboarding, then Salma's voice plays under 60 s, the pilot plays under 45 s after intake, and the learner's first spoken sentence is under 5 minutes.

title: The dropped episode starts in under 2 seconds; on-demand kinds in under 30 seconds
acceptance_criteria: Given a dropped episode, when Play is tapped, then sound starts under 2 s; given a swap, return or sample, then streaming starts under 30 s.

title: The word sheet opens in under 300 ms; the word button answers in under 2 s
The after-session pass finishes within 10 minutes and tomorrow's episode is ready before the drop
acceptance_criteria: Given a session end, when the pass runs, then `session.after_pass.completed` under 10 minutes p99; given the drop time, then 95% of episodes were ready before it, and the batch falls back to on-demand at drop minus 90 minutes.

title: Cost per session under $0.60 in the beta, with a costed path to $0.35
story: As an operator, I want every session's cost measured against the $0.60 budget and the $0.64 estimate, so that the stop line ($1.00 with no plan) is never crossed unseen.
acceptance_criteria:
Given the pilot learners' production week, when rolled up, then the measured cost per session is in the exit document beside the estimate, with the levers to $0.35 each carrying a measured first column.
Given a session over $1.00, when rolled up, then it pages with the role breakdown; given p50 over $0.80 for 7 days, then it pages.
Given no plan may lose money at full use at $0.35, when prices are confirmed, then the 2 and 3 a day plans break even at $0.42 or below.

title: The sample episode costs under $0.05 and a trial under $8
Daily spend is capped and a runaway halts
acceptance_criteria: Given the daily cap, when reached, then non-live vendor calls halt and the on-call is paged; live calls finish.

title: Told, not inferred
acceptance_criteria: Given any brief, when compiled, then only confirmed, quote-backed facts appear; sensitive classes never appear unless the learner raised them; no enrichment or external lookup about a person exists in the codebase (a dependency allow-list test).

title: Deletion and export on the clock
acceptance_criteria:
Voice storage off: call audio deleted within 15 minutes of call end. Revoke: all audio within 24 hours. Export: within 72 hours while fulfilled by hand, 1 hour once automated (ADR-24.B7). Account deletion: access ends at once with no grace (ADR-24.B1), live purge within 24 hours, backups within 30 days. Trial ended unpaid: 90 days of archive access, then one email, then deletion.
Given each window, when `privacy/verify` runs daily, then a missed window pages.
due: Day-1 (audio windows automatic; deletion by runbook in 24 hours; export by hand in 72 hours); beta day 35 (2027-04-20) for the automated export and purge

title: No personal data in logs, traces or third parties beyond the register
acceptance_criteria: Given the scrub corpus, when tests run, then zero leaks; Langfuse retention is 30 days with per-user deletion; every vendor in `vendors.yaml` has a DPA or terms and a training opt-out recorded.

title: Every learner's audio under their own key
AI disclosure and the crisis protocol in every live role
acceptance_criteria: Given "are you real?", when asked of any character in any language, then a plain answer; given a crisis keyword, then step-out, quarantine and the resources card.

title: No game furniture can be built
acceptance_criteria: Given a component for a streak, points, level, percentage, chart, leaderboard or confetti, when lint runs, then the build fails; counts are plain text and monotonic.

title: Nothing reads as a correction
acceptance_criteria: Given any generated surface (episode, call, chat, proof, feed note), when the law scan runs, then no string from the corpus ("wrong", "the correct answer", "you should have said", homework phrasing) appears; the host's per-call budgets hold (1 recast per turn, 3 clarifications, 1 nudge).

title: No claim without proof
acceptance_criteria: Given any progress sentence template, when CI greps, then it resolves to a `claims` row; the first false-claim audit on 1 January shows under 5%.

title: Exactly three kinds of outbound message
acceptance_criteria: Given the codebase, when the messaging test runs, then only the drop notification, the one opt-in gap note and transactional email (sign-in code, receipts, the day-6 trial email, payment failed, export ready, account deleted) can be sent; the weekly proof sends nothing of its own; no re-engagement job exists.

title: A prompt change cannot ship without its suite
acceptance_criteria: Given a change to a prompt, bible or rule, when CI runs, then `eval-gate` runs the mapped suites and a regression beyond threshold fails the build; the release manifest records every version.

title: Calibration against a person
acceptance_criteria: Classifier precision at least 0.8 on claim-feeding tags; rater agreement about 0.7 quadratic weighted kappa; 150 to 200 double-tagged samples by the end of the beta; a human reads 10 random episodes per learner per month.

title: Coverage and variety measured on every episode
acceptance_criteria: About 95% known words for audio and 98% for text (dial per learner); no format three times in a row; cosine similarity against the last 20 under the threshold set from the pilot's "too alike" pairs.

title: No session is lost to a voice failure
acceptance_criteria: Given a live voice failure, when detected, then the call falls back to voice notes with the same host; given a voice vendor outage, then the secondary carries the same day's production.

title: A missed drop pages within 5 minutes and has a runbook
Production restored from backup once before the beta
Capacity for 50 concurrent learners at the morning peak
acceptance_criteria: Given the drop minute for 250 learners, when load-tested, then media p95 first byte under 500 ms; given 15 concurrent calls, then no degradation in reply latency.

title: Works in the learner's own language, including right-to-left
acceptance_criteria: Given Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu as the learner's language, when any screen renders, then the bidi snapshot suite passes and logical properties are used throughout (lint).

title: Usable with a screen reader and on a mid-range Android
acceptance_criteria: Lighthouse performance above 85; every control labelled; captions on the call.

title: A language opens only through the gate
acceptance_criteria: Given a language package, when marked shippable, then all five checks passed in the harness and the result page is linked from the release manifest.
depends_on: E02-S06 (English, through the Milestone 0 gate run), E02-S08 (P1, the harness for other languages)
